title: Sharp conjugate contraction for a two point law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ be measurable, and suppose $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1/2$. Assume $\mu(X=1-\lambda)=\lambda$ and $\mu(X=-\lambda)=1-\lambda$. Then $X$ is affine hypercontractive from exponent $q/(q-1)$ to exponent $2$ with parameter $\rho(q,\lambda)$, the sharp discrete hypercontractive radius; in particular, this means $X\in L^2(\mu)$, $0\le\rho(q,\lambda)<1$, and $\|a+\rho(q,\lambda)bX\|_2\le\|a+bX\|_{q/(q-1)}$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
replaced: Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $X$ be measurable on a probability space with $\Pr[X=1-\lambda]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=-\lambda]=1-\lambda$. Then $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho_*(q,\lambda)}(X)$ holds. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
